html:
The Cuban Revolution was the armed uprising that overthrew the dictator Fulgencio Batista and brought Fidel Castro to power in Cuba on 1 January 1959.

Batista had seized power in a coup in 1952. Castro's first attack, on the Moncada barracks on 26 July 1953, failed, but it gave his group its name, the 26th of July Movement. In December 1956 Castro, his brother Raúl, Che Guevara and about eighty men landed from the small yacht Granma. Most were killed or captured. The few survivors built a guerrilla army in the Sierra Maestra mountains, while city groups fought underground.

Batista's army was brutal and lost support, and the United States stopped selling him arms in 1958. After rebel victories, including Guevara's at Santa Clara, Batista fled.

The new government soon took land and foreign owned firms, clashed with the United States, and turned to the Soviet Union. After the failed Bay of Pigs invasion of 1961, Castro declared the revolution socialist. Cuba became the first communist state in the Americas and an inspiration to left wing guerrillas across Latin America.
sum: The Cuban Revolution was the armed uprising that overthrew the dictator Fulgencio Batista and brought Fidel Castro to power in Cuba on 1 January 1959.
